Question 1
?

Given the matrix B=[740−5], find a diagonal matrix D and an invertible matrix P such that D=P−1BP.

a
D=[700−5] and P=[510−4]
b
D=[700−5] and P=[−1034]
c
B is not diagonalizable
d
D=[700−5] and P=[1−103]
e
D=[7005] and P=[1−302]
Submit

decision.explanation: For option d, the columns of P are eigenvectors: B(1,0)^T=7(1,0)^T and B(-1,3)^T=(-7+12,-15)^T=-5(-1,3)^T. Thus BP=PD. Since det(P)=3≠0, P is invertible and P^{-1}BP=D.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]$,
find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}BP.$
after.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix. Since matrix $A$ is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal: 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=7\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-5$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $B.$

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=7,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}B-7I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 0 & -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-5)I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 & 4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a homogeneous system of linear equations with the matrix as above. Note, the matrix is already in row echelon form. There is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].

content.problem:
Given the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]$,
find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}BP.$
content.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix. Since matrix $A$ is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal: 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=7\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-5$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $B.$

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=7,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}B-7I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 0 & -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & -12 \\ 4 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )-4\cdot (-12) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-1 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda -1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ Since we get two distinct eigenvalues, the matrix $A$ is diagonalizable.

Now, we construct the diagonal matrix $D,$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given the matrix A=[−3−20−2], find a diagonal matrix D and an invertible matrix P such that D=P−1AP.

a
D=[−200−3] and P=[−1−301]
b
D=[−300−2] and P=[1−201]
c
D=[200−2] and P=[1−20−1]
d
D=[2003] and P=[1201]
e
D=[3002] and P=[−1−201]
Submit

decision.explanation: For option b, A(1,0)^T=−3(1,0)^T and A(−2,1)^T=(4,−2)^T=−2(−2,1)^T. Therefore AP=PD. Since det(P)=1, P is invertible, giving D=P^{-1}AP.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Given the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]$, 
find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}AP.$
after.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix. Since matrix $A$ is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal: 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=-3\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-2$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-3)I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-2)I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a homogeneous system of linear equations with the matrix as above. Note, the matrix is already in row echelon form. There is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

Step 1. We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix. Since matrix A is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal:

λ1=−3 and λ2=−2

Thus, x1 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x2=0. Hence, the general solution is [x10],x1∈R. Setting x1=1, we get the eigenvector v1=[10].
